edges.from_text: Feedback-Enriched Environments (FEEs) consistently improve performance of self‑evolving agents on long‑horizon tasks across SciWorld and BFCL benchmarks.
edges.to_text: Adding Desired Behavior and Motivation information to prompts significantly improves coding-agent performance, whereas including Environment Information or Reproduction Steps provides no measurable benefit beyond token overhead.

edges.from_text: A well‑designed semantic interface alone can unlock substantial embodied capability from foundation VLMs, removing the need for additional model capacity or embodiment‑specific pretraining.

edges.from_text: In the paired feedback studies, 30 truthful recoveries and zero neutral recoveries were observed, and the null calibration passed with 60 paired null studies, establishing a statistically significant positive feedback effect.
edges.to_text: Across both audit cases, zero recoveries were observed in 96 independent challenger episodes, yielding a finite‑sample upper bound on the recovery probability of 0.0468.

edges.from_text: The generative guard outputs an auditable analysis and a deterministic binary safety verdict that can be consumed by downstream controllers without an external judge at inference time.
edges.to_text: Generative verification repurposes the language model’s native next‑token prediction head to produce a continuous Yes/No verification score, avoiding any added classification layer and preserving pretrained representations.

edges.from_text: Recording and reusing task experience (procedures, measurements, and corrections) shortens execution time and lowers inference cost on repeated trials, and transferring such records from a stronger agent improves a weaker agent’s success rate.
edges.to_text: Imitation‑based fine‑tuning of the weaker model on expert trajectories under the evolved harness causes consistent performance regression.

edges.from_text: In the outer recursion, the model is trained with rubric‑based rewards using GRPO while the harness and evaluation rubrics remain fixed throughout the reinforcement‑learning phase.
edges.to_text: DRACO generates rubrics dynamically during training to track the policy’s evolving capability.

edges.from_text: Training the PhAI‑IDE model family (72B, 9B, 4B) on verified scientific interaction trajectories improves held‑out scientific‑code repair performance and yields gains on general‑purpose code, reasoning, and knowledge benchmarks, demonstrating positive transfer from scientific experience

edges.from_text: All 15 attacks flagged as violations by the primary Oracle are also flagged by the two alternative Oracles, demonstrating cross‑Oracle consistency.
edges.to_text: Rubric exploitability varies dramatically with the Oracle configuration: holding a generator’s rubrics, attack responses, and judge scores fixed while swapping only the Oracle yields exploitation rates of 33.3%, 75.6%, and 66.7% respectively.
